text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bourse officials from Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain discuss unified regulations. Kuwait applies strict regulations in its bourse since its formation in 1983 following the collapse of an unofficial exchange in 1982.
- Trade and Industry Ministty mulls law to encourage foreign investments, minister says.

- Parliament's legal committee approved on Wednesday a bill that would impose a health insurance scheme on foreign resident and visitors. The bill requires the approval of the full house, the cabinet and the emir before it becomes law. Kuwait offers free health services to its nationals.
- Kuwaiti criminal court sentences man to death for murder.
- U.S. food exports to Kuwait amounted to over $40 million in 1996.

- Interior Minister Sheikh Mohammad Khaled al-Sabah says ministry needs budget boost to improve security. Kuwait is trying to reduce public spending to eliminate its budget deficit by the year 2000. The Gulf Arab state projects a 1.2 billion dinars ($4.0 billion) deficit in 1996/97 (July-June) state budget.
- North Korean worker in Kuwait defects to South Korea.
